entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cedd was an Anglo-Saxon monk and bishop from the Kingdom of Northumbria (c. 650–664 AD), who played a pivotal role in shaping the Middle Angles' and East Saxons' understanding of Christianity during the Synod of Whitby (663 AD). As a key figure in the early Christianization of England, Cedd's evangelistic efforts had far-reaching consequences for the Church in England.

His significance lies in his contribution to resolving the controversy over papal authority, which led to the establishment of the Church of England. The Synod of Whitby (663 AD) was a watershed moment in English history, marking the beginning of the Christianization of the Anglo-Saxons and shaping the course of the Church in England.

Cedd's legacy extends beyond his immediate context, influencing the development of Christianity in England and beyond. He is venerated in Anglicanism, the Roman Catholic Church, and the Orthodox Church, underscoring the enduring impact of his work.
